# SPD-038 — Drop the native allow rule for running bin/spud directly

## Brief
spud settings sync writes three native Bash allow rules; the third, for the launcher run by its own path (its #! line), auto-approves a call whose interpreter runs without -I, so PYTHONPATH and user-site .pth files inherited from the shell profile can load other code before the program. Found by SPUD-032/Carola: the hook no longer vouches for that spelling (SPD-032), but the native rule still approves it without a prompt. Fix: remove the rule from cli_allow_rules in bin/spud_ledger.py, update the settings test, run settings sync on main after merge. Every prescribed python3.14 -I -S call keeps its rule.

## Size, persona and model decision
One engineer on opus (the persona's tier), no children: one rule out of settings sync's allow list and its settings tests, then Spud runs settings sync on main after merge. No Fable today (Eric's budget). Code ticket: worktree spd-038-drop-direct-launcher-rule, from main after SPD-034's merge.
